slides.title: Solid: Social Linked Data
points: Launched in **2016** by **Tim Berners-Lee** at MIT, to **separate data from the apps** that use it
Built from **Web standards**: HTTP, URIs, RDF, Linked Data Platform, OpenID Connect
Specified by the **W3C Solid Community Group**: the **Solid Protocol** (0.11) and companion specifications for identity, access control, and notifications
Since **2024**, the **W3C Linked Web Storage Working Group** turns it into a **W3C standard**
Servers: the open source **Community Solid Server**, which we use, and others

aside.alt: Solid logo: a white S in a purple hexagon

slides.title: Solid: Pods, WebIDs, and Apps
slides.alt: Diagram: three applications (photo gallery, the PITAS app of group 3, a calendar) at the top, three pods at the bottom (Alice's pod with photos and calendar, an auction house pod with auctions and registered workers, Bob's pod on his own server with photos and results); arrows show that each app reads and writes several pods, only with the owner's permission
slides.caption: A **pod** is a Web server space for one agent's data; a **WebID** is a URI that names an agent. Apps and pods are chosen independently.

slides.title: A Pod Is a Tree of Resources
slides.code:
https://solid.example.org/pitas-g3/
  profile/card#me               # WebID document
  settings/publicTypeIndex.ttl  # what lives where
  pitas/
    auctions/                   # LDP container
      a-001.ttl                 # auction record
      a-001/
        bids/                   # append-only
          b-8f2c.ttl
    workers/                    # registered workers
points: **Containers** end with `/` and list their members with `ldp:contains`
Resources are **RDF documents** (Turtle, JSON-LD) or any other file: pictures, PDFs
Every resource has **its own URI**, so data in one pod can **link to data in any other pod**

slides.title: Who May Do What? Web Access Control
points: Modes: `Read`, `Write`, `Append` (add, **never remove**) and `Control` (**change the rules**)
`acl:accessTo` is **the container itself**, `acl:default` is **inherited** by everything in it
`acl:agent` names **one WebID**; `acl:agentClass foaf:Agent` is **anyone**

callout.text: Is sovereignty about where data sits, or about who can switch it off?

points: **Jurisdiction follows the provider**, not the data center: the [US CLOUD Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house-bill/4943) (2018) reaches data stored abroad
**[Schrems II](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62018CJ0311)** (2020) struck down the EU-US Privacy Shield; its 2023 successor remains contested

Europe answers with law and infrastructure: **[GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)**, the **[Data Act](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2854/oj)**, **[Gaia-X](https://gaia-x.eu)**
**Dependency is leverage**: a few non-European hyperscalers run most of Europe's cloud

slides.title: Any Questions / Comments / Doubts / Concerns?
points: **Decoupling** is a design choice: fix what never changes, couple only on that
**Affordances** guide people, **hypermedia** guides clients: the next action is found at run time
**Link relation types** and **media types** say why to follow a link and how to read the result
**Solid** decouples data from apps: **pods** that owners control, found from a **WebID**
**Digital sovereignty**: who can switch your data off, and whose rules apply?
